## From a title to an explanation {auto-animate="true"}

<h3 data-id="intro-title" style="text-align:left">A processor is a pipeline</h3>

::: {.fragment .sa-enter-up}
- Fetch the instruction.
:::

::: {.fragment .sa-enter-up}
- Decode the operation.
:::

::: {.fragment .sa-enter-up}
- Execute and commit the result.
:::

## A pipeline, one stage at a time

::: {.sa-cards style="grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);margin-top:1.2em"}

::: {.sa-card .fragment .sa-enter-up}
**01 — Fetch**

<small>Retrieve the instruction at the program counter.</small>
:::

::: {.sa-card .fragment .sa-enter-up}
**02 — Decode**

<small>Identify the operation and its source operands.</small>
:::

::: {.sa-card .fragment .sa-enter-up}
**03 — Execute**

<small>Compute the result using the selected functional unit.</small>
:::

:::

## MOS capacitor regimes {#mos-regimes}

For a p-type substrate; voltages relative to flat band (idealized).

::: {.sa-cards}

::: {.sa-card .fragment .custom .sa-focus}
**01　Accumulation**　 <small>\(V_G < V_{FB}\)</small>

<small>The gate attracts majority carriers. Holes crowd the surface.</small>
:::

::: {.sa-card .fragment .custom .sa-focus}
**02　Depletion**　 <small>\(V_{FB}<V_G<V_{TH}\)</small>

<small>Holes are repelled. Ionized acceptors remain in the depletion region.</small>
:::

::: {.sa-card .fragment .custom .sa-focus}
**03　Inversion**　 <small>\(V_G>V_{TH}\)</small>

<small>Electrons accumulate at the surface, forming an n-type channel.</small>
:::

:::

## Small-signal approximation {#small-signal}

A nonlinear transfer characteristic is locally linear near its bias point.

<svg class="sa-svg" viewBox="0 0 1040 380" role="img" aria-label="Nonlinear characteristic and tangent with synchronized input and output sine signals">
<g stroke="currentColor" opacity=".35" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"><path d="M65 30 V300 H480 M575 30 V155 H1000 M575 200 V325 H1000"/><path d="M575 92 H1000 M575 262 H1000" stroke-dasharray="4 5"/></g>
<g font-size="17"><text x="70" y="20">Normalized current</text><text x="430" y="320">VGS</text><text x="575" y="20">Input vgs</text><text x="575" y="190">Output Δid</text><text x="970" y="350">t</text></g>
<path id="transfer" fill="none" stroke="#3977a8" stroke-width="3"/>
<path id="tangent" fill="none" stroke="#c67e6a" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="7 5"/>
<path id="projection" fill="none" stroke="#888" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/>
<circle id="q-dot" r="6" fill="#222"/><circle id="signal-dot" r="7" fill="#c67e6a"/>
<path id="input-wave" fill="none" stroke="#3977a8" stroke-width="3"/>
<path id="output-wave" fill="none" stroke="#3977a8" stroke-width="3"/>
<path id="linear-wave" fill="none" stroke="#c67e6a" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-dasharray="7 5"/>
<circle id="input-dot" r="5" fill="#c67e6a"/><circle id="output-dot" r="5" fill="#c67e6a"/>
<g font-size="16"><text x="90" y="350" fill="#3977a8">Blue: exact square law</text><text x="290" y="350" fill="#c67e6a">Dashed: tangent</text><text id="amp-label" x="575" y="375"/></g>
</svg>

<span class="fragment sa-trigger" data-fragment-index="0"></span>
<span class="fragment sa-trigger" data-fragment-index="1"></span>
<span class="fragment sa-trigger" data-fragment-index="2"></span>
<span class="fragment sa-trigger" data-fragment-index="3"></span>

<small>Click to excite the device, reduce the amplitude, then sweep through positive and negative phases. \(I_D=kV_{OV}^2/2\), \(g_m=kV_{OV}\); normalized \(k=2,\ V_{OV,Q}=1\).</small>

<script>
(function(){
 const init=()=>{
 const m=window.SlideAnimations,svg=document.querySelector('#small-signal svg');
 if(!m||!svg||svg.dataset.bound)return;svg.dataset.bound='1';
 const get=id=>svg.querySelector('#'+id), xy=(x,y)=>[65+207*x,300-72*y], f=x=>Math.max(0,x)**2;
 const make=(n,fn)=>Array.from({length:n},(_,i)=>{const [x,y]=fn(i/(n-1));return (i?'L':'M')+x.toFixed(2)+' '+y.toFixed(2)}).join(' ');
 const set=(id,a)=>m.attrs(get(id),a), point=(id,p)=>set(id,{cx:p[0],cy:p[1]});
 set('transfer',{d:make(150,p=>xy(2*p,f(2*p)))});
 set('tangent',{d:make(2,p=>xy(.5+p,2*(.5+p)-1))});point('q-dot',xy(1,1));
 m.bindState(svg,{initial:{a:0,phase:0},steps:[
 {index:0,state:{a:.35,phase:Math.PI/2}},
 {index:1,state:{a:.1,phase:Math.PI/2}},
 {index:2,state:{a:.1,phase:Math.PI*1.5}},
 {index:3,state:{a:.1,phase:Math.PI*2.5}}
 ],duration:850,render:({a,phase})=>{
 const v=a*Math.sin(phase), q=xy(1+v,f(1+v));point('signal-dot',q);
 set('projection',{d:'M65 '+q[1]+' H'+q[0]+' V300'});
 const vin=p=>a*Math.sin(4*Math.PI*p+phase), out=p=>f(1+vin(p))-1;
 set('input-wave',{d:make(160,p=>[575+425*p,92-145*vin(p)])});
 set('output-wave',{d:make(160,p=>[575+425*p,262-78*out(p)])});
 set('linear-wave',{d:make(160,p=>[575+425*p,262-78*2*vin(p)])});
 point('input-dot',[575,92-145*v]);point('output-dot',[575,262-78*(f(1+v)-1)]);
 get('amp-label').textContent='Amplitude: '+a.toFixed(2)+' V   |   instantaneous nonlinear error: '+(v*v).toFixed(3);
 svg.dataset.amplitude=String(a);
 }});
 };
 if(window.Reveal?.isReady())init();else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',()=>{if(window.Reveal?.isReady())init();else window.Reveal?.on('ready',init);});
})();
</script>

## Matplotlib • sinusoidal input {.magic-move}

```{python}
#| label: mpl-before
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams.update({'svg.hashsalt':'slide-animations','svg.fonttype':'none','font.size':14})
t=np.linspace(0,2*np.pi,181)
def wave(phase):
    fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(9,3.6))
    ax.plot(t,np.sin(t+phase),color='#3977a8',lw=3,label='Input')
    ax.plot(t,-0.7*np.sin(t+phase),color='#c67e6a',lw=3,label='Output')
    ax.set(xlim=(0,2*np.pi),ylim=(-1.2,1.2),xlabel='Time',ylabel='Normalized voltage')
    ax.grid(alpha=.18); ax.legend(loc='upper right'); fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
wave(0)
```

## Matplotlib • phase advances {.magic-move}

```{python}
#| label: mpl-after
wave(np.pi/2)
```

## A plot is still a plot

Magic Move works with successive SVG figures. No new graphing API is required.

Keep the axes, colors and plotting order stable so that the matcher can establish correspondence.

## Seaborn • initial latency budget {.magic-move}

```{python}
#| label: sns-before
import seaborn as sns
sns.set_theme(style='whitegrid',context='talk')
def latency(values):
    fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5,3.6))
    sns.barplot(x=['Fetch','Decode','Execute','Memory'],y=values,color='#3977a8',ax=ax)
    ax.set(ylim=(0,6),ylabel='Latency (ns)',xlabel='');fig.tight_layout();plt.show()
latency([2,2.5,5,3])
```

## Seaborn • optimized execute stage {.magic-move}

```{python}
#| label: sns-after
latency([2,2.5,3,3])
```

## Algebra follows the picture

::: magic-move

$$I_D=\frac{k}{2}(V_{OV}+v_{gs})^2$$

$$I_D=\frac{k}{2}V_{OV}^2+kV_{OV}v_{gs}+\frac{k}{2}v_{gs}^2$$

$$\Delta I_D\approx g_m v_{gs}$$

:::

The approximation drops the second-order term only when the excitation is sufficiently small.

## Code retains its identity

::: magic-move

```verilog
assign y = a & b;
```

```verilog
assign y = (a & b) | c;
```

```verilog
always_comb begin
    y = (a & b) | c;
end
```

:::
